title: Chapter 203: I Saw It Myself
html:
Their shoulders brushed as they passed. Chen Ge turned to look after her. A strange scent clung to the woman—not perfume, but something closer to hospital disinfectant.

“Hey!” Chen Ge called from the elevator. The woman stopped and turned. A pair of beautiful, bewildered eyes blinked through the narrow gap between her mask and cap. They did not match the police photograph; she did not appear to be Patient No. 2.

“Are you that actress from the movie? Could I take a picture with you?” Realizing he had acted rashly, Chen Ge improvised the first excuse that came to mind.

“I’m sorry, but you have the wrong person.” Her voice was soft and sickly. She turned away and, apparently taking Chen Ge for a creep, almost broke into a jog.

She doesn’t match the photograph, but Patient No. 2 has Dorian Gray Syndrome and has undergone extensive plastic surgery. I can’t rely on appearance alone.

Modern surgery made changing one’s face entirely possible. To be safe, Chen Ge grabbed his backpack and hurried after her.

He followed her out of Building Three and into the underground parking garage, but by the time he searched the rows of cars, she had vanished.

“Where did she go?” Cameras covered the garage, and rather than risk attracting security’s attention, Chen Ge abandoned the pursuit and returned to Building Three. He rode to the fourteenth floor and knocked on Wang Xin’s door.

“Is someone there?”

Slippered footsteps approached, and the door opened. “Who are you looking for?”

A middle-aged woman in a black-and-white suit stood beyond it. Immaculately groomed, with smooth skin, she looked far younger than her age.

“It’s me. I helped Wang Xin last time…”

Before he could finish, recognition lit her face. “Doctor Chen! Please come in. I’ve wanted to thank you in person but never had the chance.”

“Doctor Chen?” The title felt strange, yet oddly familiar, despite being the first time anyone had used it. “I’m not actually a doctor.”

“To me, you’re the finest doctor because you saved Wang Xin’s life. Don’t be modest. Doctor Gao has told me so many good things about you. Please, come in!” She practically dragged him inside.

“Sorry to intrude. I came to see how Wang Xin was doing and ask you a few questions.”

“There are apples and bananas on the table. Sit down while I make some tea.”

“Please don’t trouble yourself.” Chen Ge sat on the sofa. Visiting Wang Xin was partly an excuse; his true goals were finding Patient No. 2 and completing the Tape Ghost’s affection mission. Naturally, he would not tell Wang Xin’s mother. He had an image to maintain.

As they spoke, the bedroom door opened and a slender girl emerged. Though only a few days had passed, Wang Xin looked noticeably better. Previously, she could not have left her room; now she came out to greet him of her own accord.

She had once bared her heart to him. Chen Ge still remembered every word she had spoken while clutching the Pen Spirit’s pen and weeping. Seeing her improvement brought him genuine happiness.

Wang Xin sat opposite him. Still unused to conversation, she spoke barely above a whisper. Doctor Gao had taught Chen Ge how to talk with patients, so he listened without interrupting and tried to understand her perspective.

Little by little, a smile blossomed on her face. Freed from the burden in her heart, she was learning to engage with the outside world again. After Wang Xin withdrew, her mother returned with tea. “That child keeps so much inside and never tells us anything. She can smile like this only because you’re here.”

Chen Ge accepted the cup without drinking. “Wang Xin is recovering well. The treatment is clearly helping.”

He checked the time. “Actually, there’s something I need to ask you.”

“Go ahead.” The woman readily agreed.

“I hear one of the buildings in Fang Hwa Apartments is haunted? Is that true?”

The woman’s expression froze. She rose, crept to Wang Xin’s door, and listened before leading Chen Ge into the kitchen. Once the door was closed, she said, “Doctor Chen, I’m telling you the truth. It’s real.”

“It’s truly haunted?” Chen Ge had not expected such unequivocal confirmation.

“I saw it myself.” She pointed downward. “It happened in this building, on the thirteenth floor.”

The mention of the thirteenth floor reminded Chen Ge of the woman from the elevator. Without prompting, Wang Xin’s mother continued. “Fang Hwa Apartments was built about twenty years ago. At first, it consisted only of the six older buildings in front. The three towers behind them went up four or five years ago, and I was among the first residents to move in.”

Holding her teacup, she recounted the strange events of two or three years earlier. Her story matched Uncle Wong’s, but carried greater terror: she had personally found the white figure pressed against her door.

That night, scratching outside the door had awakened her. At first she assumed it was a stray puppy or kitten, but then someone began to speak. Fearing a burglar, she fetched a cleaver from the kitchen and peered through the peephole.

The corridor’s sound-activated lights appeared broken; all she could see was a pale blur. She called the police, then struck the inside of the door with the cleaver until the white figure fled.

Her description of its escape matched Uncle Wong’s. The figure moved with astonishing speed, yet made no footsteps.

“I don’t know what it was, but the police said it was a psychiatric patient playing a prank.” She set down her cup and sighed. “I bought this apartment with a mortgage and put my life savings into it. Otherwise, I would have moved long ago.”

“You saw the white figure at close range?” As Chen Ge considered her story, his gaze passed over her remarkably youthful face and black-and-white pantsuit.

He did not distrust Wang Xin’s adoptive mother, but her preference for black and white intrigued him. At their first meeting, she had also worn a white blouse and black trousers.
